content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge resolves a collision involving the defender's and challenger's chains over Acts 2:30 by asking whether the text itself names whose body is the channel, so K-C governs the required chain-by-footing method.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the text names the seed of David 'according to the flesh' without naming whose body is the channel, so the point stays open.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "never verse by verse / stating-verse test: one reading forbids deciding by whether a single pressed verse states the point in its own words, while the other allows noting that the verse leaves a term unstated; I read K-C as requiring chain-against-chain footing rather than this verse-level indeterminacy.", "why": "The judge found Acts 2:30 underdetermined because that verse itself does not name whose body is the channel, which is the retired stating-verse/verse-by-verse test rather than weighing the competing chains by footing."}
